subtitle: The mystic who walked naked through a valley of kings and saints, leaving only words that no one could contain.

panels.shot: wide, misty valley view with a small lone figure walking along a river, mountains looming and temples and shrines faint in the distance
panels.action: Lal Ded walks along the banks of the Jhelum in the Kashmir valley, bare-limbed and unarmoured, her eyes distant, as snow peaks, temple spires and simple village roofs rise behind her in soft mist.

dialogue.text: In fourteenth-century Kashmir, amid kings, Shaiva ascetics and early Sufi saints, a woman named Lal Ded walked away from home and spoke poems no community could fully claim.

i18n.hi: चौदहवीं सदी के कश्मीर में, राजाओं, शैव साधुओं और शुरुआती सूफी संतों के बीच, लल डेड़ नाम की एक औरत घर छोड़कर चली और ऐसे वाख बोले जिन्हें कोई बिरादरी अपना कह न पाई।

panels.shot: slow push-in from high-angle over Pandrethan area, showing river, fields and an old stone temple
panels.action: The camera glides over early-medieval Pandrethan near Srinagar: terraced fields, the stone shrine by the river, smoke from village homes; Lal Ded stands small near a doorway, half in shadow.

dialogue.text: The records are late and hazy, but they point to a Kashmiri girl born near Srinagar, in a land of stone temples, village shrines, Naga springs and Sanskrit-learning houses.

i18n.hi: दस्तावेज़ देर के और धुंधले हैं, मगर वे श्रीनगर के पास जन्मी एक कश्मीरी लड़की की ओर इशारा करते हैं, पत्थर के मंदिरों, गांव–देवस्थान, नागा–झरनों और संस्कृत सीखने वाले घरों की धरती पर।

panels.shot: medium shot inside a modest Kashmiri household, low light, Lal Ded seated on the floor, listening to chanting outside
panels.action: Inside a dark wooden house, Lal Ded sits by a hearth, her face turned to a small lattice window where older men chant softly, their voices carrying from a neighbouring Shaiva prayer hall.

dialogue.text: From family homes like this came women who heard mantra and philosophy through walls, while men studied scriptures. Tradition remembers Lal Ded among those who refused to stay just listeners.

i18n.hi: इन्हीं घरों से वे औरतें निकलीं जो दीवारों के पार से मंत्र और दर्शन सुनती थीं, जबकि मर्द शास्त्र पढ़ते थे। रस्में लल डेड़ को उन में गिनती हैं जिन्होंने सिर्फ सुनने से इंकार किया।

panels.shot: low-angle interior courtyard, Lal Ded in simple clothing turning away from domestic tools toward an open gate and sky
panels.action: In a small courtyard, grinding stone and water pots lie abandoned as Lal Ded, in rough homespun, stands upright and looks toward the open gate, where bright valley light spills in.

dialogue.text: Stories speak of a harsh marriage and mockery at home, but historians cannot fix names and faces. What is clear is that she walked away from domestic duties into the life of a renouncer.

i18n.hi: कहानियां सख्त शादी और घर की ठट्ठों की बताती हैं, पर इतिहास नाम–चेहरे तय नहीं कर पाता। इतना साफ है कि वह चूल्हा–चौका छोड़कर विरागिन की राह पर चल पड़ी।

panels.shot: epic wide shot of a Kashmiri path with river and poplars, Lal Ded walking, small figures staring from a distance
panels.action: On a dusty path lined with poplars and willows by the Jhelum, villagers pause in surprise as Lal Ded strides past, her body barely covered, her movement steady, eyes unafraid.

dialogue.text: Lal Ded stepped into the open, shedding the markers of modest household womanhood. Legend says she moved half-naked, a shock in fourteenth-century Kashmir, her body itself a refusal.

i18n.hi: लल डेड़ खुले आसमान में आ गई, सुथरी गृहिणी के सब निशान उतार फेंके। दंतकथा कहती है, वह अधनंगी चली–फिरती थी; चौदहवीं सदी के कश्मीर में खुद उसका जिस्म ही एक इंकार था।

panels.shot: close-up on Lal Ded’s face in prayerful focus, background shows faint outline of Shaiva yogis by a shrine
panels.action: Lal Ded sits near a shrine under a chinar tree, her spine straight, hands resting on her knees, while in soft focus Shaiva ascetics perform ritual nearby, wrapped in wool and ash.

dialogue.text: Kashmiri Shaiva practice, older than the Sultans, shaped her inner world. Her vakhs speak of breath, mind and awareness, echoing yogic discipline yet spoken in everyday Kashmiri speech.

i18n.hi: कश्मीर का पुराना शैव साधन, सुल्तानों से भी पहले का, उसके भीतर का जग गढ़ता गया। उसके वाख सांस, मन और जागरूकता की बात करते हैं, योग–अनुशासन की गूंज लिए, मगर रोज़मर्रा की कश्मीरी ज़बान में।

panels.shot: medium shot at a village square, Lal Ded addressing a small gathered crowd, children and elders, with animated gesture
panels.action: In a village square, mud houses around, Lal Ded stands on a worn stone, palm raised, reciting to farmers, women and children who lean in, their faces lit by interest and unease.

dialogue.text: “Do not wander from forest to shrine; the One you seek sits inside your own chest.”

i18n.hi: “जंगल से देवस्थान तक मत भटको; जिसे ढूंढ रही हो, वही तेरे सीने के भीतर बैठा है।”

panels.shot: extreme close-up of Lal Ded’s mouth mid-utterance, background blurred, sense of sound hanging in the air
panels.action: The image freezes on Lal Ded’s lips as she speaks, the wrinkles at their edges showing age and travel; the background is a soft blur of chinar leaves and listening faces.

dialogue.text: Her sayings, the vakhs, travelled first by voice. No one wrote them down in her time; they passed from tongue to ear, shaped by the accents and needs of each retelling.

i18n.hi: उसकी बातें, उसके वाख, पहले जुबानी चले। उसके समय किसी ने उन्हें लिखा नहीं; वे ज़बान से कान तक घूमे, हर दोहराव में बोलियों और ज़रूरतों के साथ थोड़ा–थोड़ा ढलते गए।

panels.shot: wide shot of Srinagar’s waterways with old wooden houses, Lal Ded walking along a bank, distant sight of mosque and temple
panels.action: Along Srinagar’s riverfront of wooden houses and carved balconies, Lal Ded walks as boatmen ferry passengers; on the horizon, the silhouette of a temple stands near the rising shape of a mosque.

dialogue.text: When she lived, Kashmir was shifting. Old Hindu dynasties gave way to the Shah Mir Sultanate. Temples and new mosques shared the skyline, while Sufi lodges joined Shaiva hermitages.

i18n.hi: जब वह जीती थी, कश्मीर बदल रहा था। पुराने हिंदू वंशों की जगह शाह मीर सुल्तनत उठ रही थी। मंदिर और नई मस्जिदें एक ही आसमान में थीं, सूफी खानकाहें शैव तपो–स्थान के साथ जुड़ती गईं।

panels.shot: balanced wide shot showing Shaiva ascetics on one side of a shrine courtyard and Sufi figures on the other, Lal Ded passing between
panels.action: In a stone courtyard, Shaiva ascetics sit cross-legged to one side, cloaked Sufi seekers to the other; Lal Ded walks calmly between them, bare feet on cold rock, gaze turned inward.

dialogue.text: Later, Shaivas hailed her as Lalleshwari, a yogini of their lineage. Muslims cherished her as Lal Arifa, a knowing friend of God. Both found their values reflected in her rough-spun wisdom.

i18n.hi: बाद में शैवों ने उसे लल्लेश्वरी कहा, अपने सिलसिले की योगिनी। मुसलमानों ने उसे लाल अरिफ़ा के नाम से चाहा, ख़ुदा की जानकार दोस्त। दोनों को उसकी खुरदरी समझ में अपनी क़ीमतें झलकती दिखीं।

panels.shot: slow push-in on a group of villagers near a fire at dusk, one elder reciting a vakh attributed to Lal Ded, silhouettes
panels.action: At dusk, villagers huddle around a small fire; an elder, face lit by embers, recites one of Lal Ded’s vakhs as others listen, their silhouettes framed by chinar trunks and mountain dusk.

dialogue.text: Her lines lived where people gathered: by river banks, in winter rooms, on pilgrimage routes. With each generation, words shifted slightly, turning memory itself into an editor.

i18n.hi: उसकी पंक्तियां वहीं जीती रहीं जहाँ लोग जुटते थे: नदी किनारों पर, जाड़े की क़हवा–कमरों में, ज़ियारत–रास्तों पर। हर पीढ़ी के साथ शब्द ज़रा–ज़रा सरके, याद को ही नए सिरे से संगठित करते रहे।

panels.shot: interior of a Persianate scholar’s study centuries later, manuscripts piled, scholar writing, faint superposed image of Lal Ded
panels.action: In a later age, a Persianate scholar sits in a lamp-lit room, copying from an older text into a neat manuscript, while a faint, ghostlike image of Lal Ded hovers above his desk.

dialogue.text: Centuries passed before her name entered written chronicles like Tadhkirat-ul-Arifin and Waqiati-e-Kashmir. By then, history and legend had tangled around her like thick valley mist.

i18n.hi: सदियां बीत गईं तब जाकर उसका नाम तज़किरत–उल–आरिफ़ीन और वाक़िआती–ए–कश्मीर जैसे लिखित इतिहासों में घुसा। तब तक दास्तान और ताबरी दोनों उसके चारों ओर घाटी की घनी धुंध–से उलझ चुके थे।

panels.shot: symbolic wide shot: Lal Ded seated beside a cradle under a tree, Nund Rishi as a baby in cradle, scene bathed in unreal light
panels.action: Under a vast chinar tree, Lal Ded sits beside a simple cradle, a baby inside, as villagers watch from a respectful distance; the scene glows in gentle, symbolic light, unreal and dreamlike.

dialogue.text: One beloved tale says she nursed the infant Nund Rishi, future Kashmiri saint. Historians treat this as legend, a poetic way to show how her spirit fed later traditions of devotion.

i18n.hi: एक प्यारी दास्तान कहती है कि उसने नुंद ऋषि, उस नवजात भावी संत को दूध पिलाया। इतिहासकार इसे क़िस्सा मानते हैं, एक शायराना ढंग से यह दिखाने को कि उसकी रूह ने बाद की भक्ति–धाराओं को भी पोसा।

panels.shot: medium shot of Lal Ded in old age walking along a snowy path, mountains sharp, her figure lean but firm
panels.action: An older Lal Ded walks on a thin snowy path, her body lean, ribs faintly visible beneath her wrap, yet her stride strong, snow crunching under calloused feet, breath rising in the cold air.

dialogue.text: Renunciation for her was not metaphor. She embraced hunger, cold and insult. Yet her vakhs do not glorify suffering; they point again and again to clarity of mind and kindness of heart.

i18n.hi: उसके लिए विराग सिर्फ रूपक नहीं था। उसने भूख, ठंड और ताने गले लगाए। फिर भी उसके वाख दुख को महिमा नहीं देते; वे बार–बार साफ़ दिमाग और नरम दिल की ओर इशारा करते हैं।

panels.shot: close-up of Lal Ded looking directly at viewer, half-smile, valley reflected in her eyes
panels.action: Lal Ded turns toward us, face lined and open, a small half-smile on her lips; in her dark eyes, the reflection of river, field, temple and mosque appears together.

dialogue.text: “Who am I? Ask not my name. Look instead for the witness within you.”

i18n.hi: “मैं कौन हूँ? मेरा नाम मत पूछो। अपने भीतर बैठे गवाह को ढूंढो।”

panels.shot: montage wide shot: overlapping images of Hindu devotees, Muslim faqirs, modern readers all holding or hearing her vakhs
panels.action: A layered image shows a Shaiva devotee at a spring, a Sufi faqir in a khanqah, and a modern Kashmiri reader by electric light, all holding or hearing fragments of Lal Ded’s poetic lines.

dialogue.text: Today, her words sit in printed books, travel in Kashmiri songs, and stir debates over identity. Scholars like Jayalal Kaul, Ranjit Hoskote and Mridu Rai trace how politics reshapes her image.

i18n.hi: आज उसके शब्द छपे किताबों में हैं, कश्मीरी गीतों में फिरते हैं, और पहचान पर बहसें जगाते हैं। जयलाल कौल, रंजीत होस्कोटे और मृदु राय जैसे विद्वान देखते हैं कि सियासत उसके चेहरों को कैसे बदलती रहती है।

panels.shot: final sweeping aerial shot over the Kashmir valley at sunrise, a tiny figure of Lal Ded walking dissolves into the landscape
panels.action: At sunrise, the camera drifts high above the Kashmir valley, rivers gleaming and villages waking; below, the faint figure of Lal Ded walking slowly fades until the land itself seems to carry her.

dialogue.text: We cannot pin Lal Ded to one sect, village or story, but her Kashmiri voice still crosses those boundaries, reminding us that some truths belong first to a place and only then to its labels.

i18n.hi: हम लल डेड़ को किसी एक मज़हब, गांव या कहानी में नहीं बाँध सकते, पर उसकी कश्मीरी आवाज़ आज भी इन सीमाओं को पार करती है, याद दिलाती है कि कुछ सच पहले ज़मीन के होते हैं, बाद में उसके नाम–पट्टों के।

title_i18n.hi: लल डेड़ कश्मीर में चलती है

subtitle_i18n.en: The mystic who walked naked through a valley of kings and saints, leaving only words that no one could contain.
subtitle_i18n.hi: वह फकीर जो राजाओं और संतों की घाटी में नंगी चली, पीछे बस ऐसे शब्द छोड़ गई जिन्हें कोई थाम न सका।
